content.value_statement: Next.js App Router work often requires precise file structure and component boundaries. This skill guides page, layout, route, and dashboard implementation with Server Component defaults.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of App Router pages with metadata, Suspense, and loading states.
Explains dynamic route patterns with params, metadata generation, and not-found handling.
Separates Server Component and Client Component responsibilities for common React tasks.
Covers nested layouts, templates, route groups, parallel routes, and intercepting routes.
Provides role-based dashboard patterns for admin, teacher, and student experiences.
Shows shadcn/ui, chart, error boundary, and route handler usage patterns.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not run builds or tests by itself.
Example data functions and authentication helpers must be implemented in the target project.
It focuses on the App Router and does not cover legacy Pages Router architecture.
It does not choose database schemas, hosting platforms, or authentication providers.

use_cases.title: Create Dashboard Pages
use_cases.description: Build App Router dashboard pages with Server Components, metadata, loading states, and reusable layouts.

use_cases.title: Plan Dynamic Routes
use_cases.description: Design profile, task, course, or product routes with params, 404 behavior, and page-specific metadata.
use_cases.target_user: Full-stack developers adding routed product features

use_cases.title: Structure Role-Based ERP Views
use_cases.description: Create admin, teacher, and student dashboards with role checks, navigation layouts, and chart components.
use_cases.target_user: Teams building education or operations platforms

prompt_templates.title: Create A Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Next.js App Router dashboard page with metadata, a loading state, and Server Component data fetching. Explain which files to add.

prompt_templates.title: Add Dynamic Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a dynamic student profile route using the App Router. Include params handling, metadata generation, and not-found behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Separate Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this App Router feature and separate Server Components from Client Components. Keep client code only where interactivity is required.

prompt_templates.title: Design Role Dashboards
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an App Router structure for admin, teacher, and student dashboards. Include layouts, route groups, role guards, loading states, and chart boundaries.

output_examples.input: Create an admin dashboard page for a school ERP system.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a file plan for the dashboard route, layout, role guard, data boundary, loading state, and chart component split.

output_examples.input: Add a student profile route with SEO metadata.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a dynamic route, params handling, metadata lookup, missing-student behavior, and a reusable profile view component.

output_examples.input: Move a form into the correct App Router component type.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies which part stays server-rendered and which form controls need a Client Component boundary.

best_practices: Use Server Components by default and add Client Components only for browser APIs, hooks, or event handlers.
Define loading, error, not-found, and metadata behavior near the route that owns the user experience.
Keep route groups, layouts, and templates aligned with the application navigation model.
anti_patterns: Do not use client-side effects for initial data loading when a Server Component can fetch the data.
Do not place broad client boundaries around pages that only need small interactive controls.
Do not create dynamic routes without clear missing-record handling and metadata behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill support the Next.js App Router?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on the App Router, including pages, layouts, templates, route groups, and dynamic routes.

faq.question: Can it help with Server and Client Components?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when to keep logic on the server and when client interactivity requires a Client Component.

faq.question: Does it generate complete production applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples that must be integrated with the project codebase.

faq.question: Can it help with role-based dashboards?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for admin, teacher, and student dashboards with role checks and layouts.

faq.question: Does it cover route handlers?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes route handler examples for common API patterns in App Router projects.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is declared for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
